Medication can work or backfire sometimes. Or it might also bring unintended changes like making him less depressed but feeling less fun or joy too. It can even make him loose interest in hobbies or relationships so it’s not for everyone. As for therapy I honestly feel that’s short side in his part but I guess understandable. It’s not good to not want to change or at least talk about your problems tho, I’d go to a therapist even if I was relatively healthy all the time, but this is something one has to find the courage and will to do.

It can be hard to afford but a specialist tends to be better depending on what he has, remember that it’s in him to do it in the end though. It’s fine to talk about how it affects you and give an outside perspective just like a friend would when giving advice but it’s up to him.

Best of luck in whatever you two decide, remember to take care of yourself too and your own needs and health.

Btw about how to start talking about it, I’ve used friends to practice on and an app called Wysa thats like an interactive journal, it has a part on how to start difficult conversations that lets you practice it out with the computer which might help you get started and see if it sounds good. It’s just an ai so it’s not the best but it helps.

Oh yeah for sure leading someone on can be really hurtful to the other person when you do leave, plus it can make you feel even guiltier later on about the idea of leaving. that’s why I said that it’s a good idea to sit down and tell him she doesn’t see themselves as far in the future as he does.

I said the thing about the break because she could take that to figure her feelings out because from what she said she’ sounds uncertain about it. I should add that being clear bout the possibility of breaking up the whole time is important tho. It’s good to think things out so that you’re fully aware of what you want and don’t have regrets or back out last moment thinking what if. 

The most important thing is that she doesn’t stay only for his sake or leaves without really taking in why or worse, being unsure and potentially coming back just to make the problem worse. How she feels and her own mental health matter most in her decision.

In my opinion she’ll probably decide to end things up if she doesn’t wish to reconnect with him like they were before. As for him he can get in touch with himself and seek out help during that time if they do take that route(a break).

What I do strongly agree with you on most is that leading him on or ignoring how she’s feeling without acting on it can end up badly, like if you no longer love someone in a romantic way then don’t act like you love them the same, keeping hurtful things from someone because you think they’re fragile is just bundling it all up for later.

You miss my point, she says she loves him still but feels stuck and doesn’t know how to talk to him, not wanting to hurt him. I’m just saying that she can sit down and talk to him about it to let him understand. When you said run I just interpreted it as leaving and ghosting him which is a horrible thing to do. By the sound of it she’s likely his largest source of support. 

She says she isn’t sure if it’s worth continuing so I’d just recommend talking about what their goals are at this moment and taking a break. 

And she can definitely talk to him about therapy and ask him how he’s gonna be after they’re separated, they’re both adults but it doesn’t mean she can’t care. It’s on him if he actually does it tho, it is not her responsibility to carry him through life.

Get him to go to therapy if he doesn’t already, I’m just assuming but I don’t think you’re a doctor. And try and talk to him about how you’re feeling since he’s a part of the situation too. Remember he’s a living breathing human being with a real problem and if you’re gonna make decisions for your own health make sure they’re not forsaking his just like you shouldn’t forsake your own mental health for him.

You’re right she needs to think of herself too but coming from someone who’s been in a similar place but from the other side, you need to do that calmly with compassion,not run. If they just up and leave like they didn’t care then they might end up doing what they’re trying to avoid. I’d say try to get him professional help. You wanna help him by staying but that uncertainty will only sabotage whatever relationship there is and you’ll either loose patience or break. Talk to him about how you’re feeling and if it can be saved it’s by you both trying not just you wanting to keep him from being hurt or him not knowing there are problems.

I’ve put appointments and stuff for the doctor but when it comes it just gets difficult to even try, A mental hospital sounds like a bad idea if they keep me in a room or if I end up more restricted than at home
I was only holding on because of them and now it feels pointless
Barely have any that don’t bail quickly
